title: TP hang repro notes (WIP) — mixed prefill/decode + streaming
linked_artifacts: GitHub: benchmark-lab PR-97 (tp hang repro harness — mixed workload)
content:
Doc purpose
- Capture messy, iterative notes for reproducing the tensor-parallel (TP) hang/stall under sustained mixed workload.
- This is NOT a polished RCA. Goal is: deterministic-ish repro + artifact pointers (logs/traces) + quick hypotheses.

Quick status (as of 2025-03-01)
- We can reproduce a TP stall on A100 80GB (8x) in benchmark-lab using a mixed prefill/decode distribution + streaming clients.
- Repro rate ranges from ~10–40% per 30-min run depending on concurrency and whether prefix caching is enabled.
- Current most consistent “signature”: scheduler-induced collective starvation / inconsistent collective sequencing across ranks when a subset of ranks stays busy in prefill while others enter decode loop.
- Secondary signature (rare but nasty): cancellation path with streaming client disconnect -> one rank exits decode loop early, other ranks block waiting on collective.

Where this started
- Dedicated customer timeouts + “hung replica” symptoms; see SUP-48344 + incident thread (sev1 2025-02-17).
- Initial repro success thread: Slack eng-runtime/1739784412.

----
Environment(s) tried

Env A: benchmark-lab / A100 80GB
- Cluster: bench-lab-a100 (internal)
- GPUs per node: 8x A100 80GB SXM
- CUDA driver: 535.xx (check nvidia-smi logs in artifact bundle)
- CUDA runtime: 12.2 (container)
- NCCL: 2.18.x (container)
- Runtime build(s):
  - runtime-1.18.7+commit(unknown) (baseline, hangs seen)
  - runtime-1.19.0-rc1 (partial fixes; hang rate lower but not zero)
- TP config: tp=4 (mostly); also saw stalls at tp=2 with different characteristics
- Model(s):
  - llama-70b-instruct (primary)
  - mixtral-8x7b (secondary; stalls rarer but still shows heartbeat gaps at high conc)

Env B: hosted staging / H100
- Harder to get clean repro due to autoscaling + noisy neighbors.
- Good for validating instrumentation and “stall reason” metrics once repro is reliable.

----
Repro recipe (current best)

High level
- Run a mixed workload with (a) long prefill prompts (8k–32k tokens) + (b) smaller prompts that enter decode quickly.
- Ensure streaming responses to keep decode iterating while new prefills arrive.
- Run at enough concurrency that scheduler interleaving pressure is sustained (not just a single large batch).

1) Benchmark-lab harness (preferred)
- Uses benchmark-lab PR-97 config: mixed workload w/ tunable seq len distribution.

Command (example)
- NOTE: this is the exact one that produced a stall on 2025-02-19, run #7.

benchctl run \
  --cluster bench-lab-a100 \
  --image redwood/runtime:1.18.7 \
  --replicas 2 \
  --gpus-per-replica 4 \
  --tp 4 \
  --model llama-70b-instruct \
  --scenario tp_mixed_prefill_decode_streaming_v3 \
  --duration 45m \
  --concurrency 96 \
  --prefill-p50 4096 --prefill-p95 24576 \
  --decode-max-new-tokens 512 \
  --streaming true \
  --client-timeout 120s \
  --rate-limit disabled

Common knobs (impact on repro)
- concurrency >= 80: increases probability.
- prefill-p95 >= 16k: increases probability.
- streaming=true: required (non-streaming still shows timeouts but less “hang-like”).
- prefix caching ON: makes it worse when cache pressure triggers compaction (see KV notes).

2) Local client against a dedicated replica (useful for cancellation signature)
- Purpose: reproduce “client disconnect/cancel” path.

Command
python tools/loadgen/streaming_chat.py \
  --endpoint http://<replica-ip>:<port>/v1/chat/completions \
  --model llama-70b-instruct \
  --concurrency 64 \
  --prompt-len-dist mixed:short=256,long=16384,long_weight=0.25 \
  --max-new-tokens 256 \
  --disconnect-rate 0.02 \
  --disconnect-after-seconds 1.5 \
  --duration-minutes 30

Expectation
- With disconnect-rate ~2%, we sometimes get a rank stuck waiting on a collective after another rank aborts decode.

----
Runtime config / flags tried

Baseline flags
- tp=4
- continuous_batching=true
- multi_stream_decode=true (when enabled by default)
- kv_cache=on (prefix caching enabled)

Useful debug toggles
- Disable CUDA graphs (to isolate capture constraints):
  - RWD_CUDA_GRAPHS=0
- Force single stream (often reduces hang probability but hurts throughput):
  - RWD_DECODE_MULTI_STREAM=0
- Force deterministic scheduler mode (experimental):
  - RWD_SCHED_DETERMINISTIC=1
- Cap batch / tokens (mitigation; reduces hang frequency):
  - RWD_MAX_BATCH_TOKENS=8192
  - RWD_MAX_CONCURRENCY=64

NCCL debug knobs (use carefully)
- Minimal signal without flooding:
  - NCCL_DEBUG=WARN
  - NCCL_DEBUG_SUBSYS=COLL
- For short windows only (perf + log volume risk):
  - NCCL_DEBUG=INFO
  - NCCL_DEBUG_SUBSYS=ALL
  - NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1
- We avoided NCCL_DEBUG=TRACE except for <5 min due to volume.

----
Observed symptoms & signatures

Signature S1: “silent stall” / no hard NCCL error
- External symptoms:
  - Requests stop making progress; streaming responses freeze.
  - p99 climbs; eventually client timeouts.
  - Replica remains “healthy” at process level (no crash), GPU utilization may drop to low/0 on one or more ranks.
- Internal symptoms (pre-instrumentation):
  - No obvious CUDA error thrown.
  - One or more ranks appear to be waiting on a stream event / collective.

Signature S2: collective mismatch / ordering divergence (suspected)
- Seen in some NCCL logs: warnings about collective “sequence” not matching across ranks (not always present).
- Hypothesis: scheduler fairness/interleaving causes one rank to enter next collective while another is still executing a previous micro-batch stage.
- Strong correlation with “prefill heavy” bursts while decode is mid-loop.

Signature S3: cancellation/disconnect path deadlock
- Triggered by streaming client disconnects.
- Hypothesis: cancellation tears down decode loop on a subset of ranks; others keep waiting for a collective to complete.
- Related to PR: redwood PR-21890 (fix deadlock on cancelled streaming requests in TP).

Signature S4: KV cache pressure/compaction amplifies stalls
- When KV cache compaction is enabled and memory pressure is high, we see increased heartbeat gaps before full stall.
- Not sure if compaction is a cause vs a multiplier (timing perturbation that makes scheduler starvation worse).
- Related: ENG-4827 and redwood PR-21866.

----
Artifacts (where logs live)

Benchmark-lab runs
- bench run ids (approx; see bench-lab UI):
  - 2025-02-19 run#7: first consistent stall in v3 scenario (A100, tp=4, conc=96)
  - 2025-02-21 run#3: stall with NCCL WARN “collective mismatch” (A100)
  - 2025-02-26 run#5: cancellation-induced stall reproduced (disconnect-rate 2%)

Log bundle naming convention (if you’re looking in shared drive)
- shared_drives/engineering/serving-runtime/artifacts/tp-repro/<YYYY-MM-DD>/<runid>/
- Contains:
  - runtime.log (structured)
  - rank*.log (per rank)
  - nccl.log (if enabled)
  - nsys traces (sometimes)
  - gpu-metrics.csv

NOTE: Some of these bundles were temporarily stored in Slack threads as snippets; longer files are in the artifacts folder above.

----
Partial findings / hypotheses (not final)

1) Scheduler starvation -> ranks desync on collective boundaries
- Evidence:
  - Stalls correlate with prefill-heavy bursts.
  - Disabling multi-stream decode reduces repro rate significantly.
  - When forcing more strict fairness / ordering (local patch), stall rate decreases.
- Working hypothesis:
  - The scheduler allows some ranks to continue consuming prefill work while others proceed into decode iteration that expects a collective alignment.
  - This can yield inconsistent ordering / one rank “waiting” at a collective while another is in a different phase.
- Related fix track:
  - ENG-4824 + redwood PR-21841.

2) Stream/event sync around NCCL collectives insufficiently strict
- Evidence:
  - Adding explicit event sync around collective launch reduced “silent stall” instances in microbench; might be masking ordering issues.
  - Some suspected cases where kernels continue on compute stream while collective stream waits (or vice versa).
- Hypothesis:
  - We have missing stream synchronization between compute and NCCL stream in a multi-stream pipeline, especially under backpressure.
- Related fix track:
  - ENG-4825 + redwood PR-21853.
- Open question:
  - How much of the stall is “true NCCL hang” vs “our streams waiting incorrectly”? Need better counters + trace spans.

3) Cancellation path needs to coordinate across ranks
- Evidence:
  - Repro with disconnect-rate > 1%.
  - After client disconnect, one rank logs “request cancelled” and frees resources; other ranks continue waiting.
- Related fix track:
  - redwood PR-21890.

4) KV cache compaction timing interacts with TP
- Evidence:
  - When memory pressure triggers compaction during a busy mixed run, heartbeats stall more often.
- Hypothesis:
  - Compaction triggers additional synchronization or changes scheduling decisions, making starvation easier.
- Related fix track:
  - ENG-4827 + redwood PR-21866.

----
Instrumentation needs (what we’re missing)

Must-have metrics to confirm root cause
- Per-rank heartbeat (monotonic step counter + timestamp) to detect gaps.
- In-flight collective counters (per rank + collective type) to see divergence.
- Scheduler queue depth + “phase” tags (prefill vs decode) and how it maps to ranks.
- Stall reason codes (compute vs comms vs scheduler vs memory).

Status
- ENG-4823 / PR-21834 in progress; naming discussed in Slack eng-runtime/1739897721.

----
Suggested next experiments

Experiment E1: Reduce to minimal toggles that reproduce S1 reliably
- Goal: remove compaction and cancellation; isolate scheduler/comms.
- Plan:
  - kv_cache=off
  - disconnect-rate=0
  - Keep mixed prefill/decode + streaming
  - Sweep conc 64/80/96

Experiment E2: Force strict collective ordering (debug build)
- Goal: validate whether ordering mismatch is the actual trigger.
- Plan:
  - Add debug assertions around collective sequencing per request id / step id
  - Emit to structured log: rank, req_id, decode_iter, collective_seq

Experiment E3: Add extra stream sync (guarded) and measure perf hit
- Goal: see if “hardening” avoids stall without unacceptable regression.
- Plan:
  - Compare tokens/sec, p50/p99 latency, and hang rate with/without sync.
  - Use microbench + the tp_mixed scenario.

Experiment E4: Cancellation barrier across ranks
- Goal: confirm PR-21890 resolves S3.
- Plan:
  - High disconnect-rate run for 15 min
  - Validate that cancellation triggers a coordinated abort vs leaving ranks waiting

----
Operational notes / mitigations (temporary)

If you need to reduce hang probability while testing
- Cap concurrency (64) and batch tokens.
- Consider disabling multi-stream decode.
- Prefer shorter p95 prefill lengths (<= 8k).

If you hit a wedged replica
- Drain/replace replica (don’t keep sending traffic).
- Capture:
  - last 5 min of runtime logs + per-rank logs
  - GPU metrics snapshot
  - Any NCCL WARN/INFO (if enabled)
- Then restart (we’ve seen “stuck until restart”).

----
Open questions
- Are we seeing a true NCCL hang, or a “logical hang” from rank divergence leading to blocked waits?
- Does CUDA graph capture make this worse (constraints on stream semantics), or is it incidental?
- How much does KV cache compaction contribute causally vs probabilistically?
- What’s the right default watchdog timeout per model size / context length without false positives? (See Slack eng-runtime/1739973309.)

Changelog (manual)
- 2025-02-10: doc created; initial env + first A100 repro summary.
- 2025-02-19: added benchmark-lab command + v3 scenario parameters.
- 2025-02-21: added NCCL WARN mismatch notes + hypotheses S2.
- 2025-02-26: added cancellation/disconnect repro path + link to PR-21890.
- 2025-03-01: consolidated signatures + next experiments; added artifact organization notes.
